William Arthur Lewis, born in St Lucia in 1915, was an economist who won the Nobel prize for economics in 1979. He was the first Black person to win a Nobel prize outside the peace prize.

His 1954 paper on development with unlimited supplies of labour described how workers move from farms to factories in poor countries. The idea, known as the dual sector model, guided planners across Asia, Africa and the Caribbean.

He advised the new government of Ghana under Kwame Nkrumah, headed the University of the West Indies and founded the Caribbean Development Bank. He taught at Princeton. With Derek Walcott, he gave tiny St Lucia two Nobel prizes.
